proposals.impact: convert 2 intro-load sessions into quiz starts
proposals.observation: In the last 48 hours, the quiz recorded 2 sessions and 0 starts. Both sessions stalled at intro_load, meaning visitors loaded the intro screen and left without pressing anything. No traffic problem exists here — 2 people found the quiz. The problem is the intro screen itself. Either the first thing they read does not pull them forward, or the CTA button is not visible without scrolling on mobile. The data shows a 0% start rate from a warm direct-traffic audience, which is a pure copy-or-layout problem on a single screen.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the quiz intro CTA copy. The current text almost certainly uses a generic promise ("Find out your money personality" or similar) that any one of a thousand coaches could have written. Replace it with something rooted in the specific, felt experience Joel's ICP recognises — the moment you earn well but still can't explain where it goes. Keep the button label short and first-person. Do not add extra steps or new components. One file, one text change.
proposals.new_text:
You earn well. So why does checking your balance still feel like a small act of bravery?

This takes four minutes. It starts with the thing you actually do with money — not the thing you mean to do.

Start the quiz

proposals.impact: replicate 66.67% open rate pattern across lower-performing automations
proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation has a 66.67% open rate across 12 sent. Money Avoidance is at 52.63% across 19 sent. Money Worship sits at 37.5% across 16 sent. The Vigilance rate is 29 percentage points above Worship. These three sequences run from the same quiz funnel to a similar audience, so the gap almost certainly lives in subject-line copy or sender-name presentation, not in list quality. The Vigilance sequence subject line is probably doing something specific and concrete that the Worship line is not.
proposals.proposal: Pull the subject line from email 1 of the Money Vigilance sequence. Identify what makes it concrete or personally addressed — a number, a specific behaviour, a named feeling. Apply that same structural logic (not the same words) to the subject line of email 1 in the Money Worship sequence. One file, one line change. Do not rewrite the body copy.
proposals.current_text: subject: You've got a complicated relationship with money — here's what that actually means
proposals.new_text: subject: You checked the price. You could afford it. You still put it back.

proposals.impact: stop content queue from stalling at 1 queued post
proposals.observation: Two CI workflows failed in the last 24 hours: "Daily Blog Post" at 06:58 and "Funnel-Hack Digest" at 11:45. The content queue now sits at 1 queued post against 47 published. If the Daily Blog Post workflow keeps failing, that single queued post is the only buffer before the queue empties. The workflow file itself is blocked from edits, but the generation script it calls is not listed as a blocked path. A silent failure with no fallback is the likely cause — the script throws when an API call returns unexpectedly, and nothing catches it to write a placeholder file instead.
proposals.proposal: Add a try/catch around the main generation call in the blog post script so that on failure it writes a minimal placeholder markdown file with a draft: true frontmatter flag. This means the workflow exits 0, the queue gets a file (invisible to the public until Joel removes the draft flag), and the failure becomes visible as a draft rather than a broken pipeline. One file, one wrapped block. Do not change the workflow YAML.
